units.title: Shop: bread back on time, biscuits for tonight
units.author: dc_2_hassan
units.text: Bread is back on time today now the fog is lifting, so no more 9 o'clock toast. For tonight's meeting I will bring two tins of biscuits and the big urn from the stockroom. Torches are still at cost price. If you are on the buddy sheet for the stairs, come and take one free. H

units.author: dc_7_irena
units.text: Dear Jordie, thank you for writing that down honestly. It is what I hear too, though I come down and you go up. Four or five more, and then nothing. Please do not stand in the dark for a minute again; come and knock, I am always awake early and my husband always said I make the best cocoa on the block. I have added your note to the list for tonight. Irena, 7C

units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: Thank you, Hassan, I will take you up on it, though only for the tins. Lift engineer now 'day 9 or day 10' according to the new sticker, which is the third sticker. I shall attend the meeting tonight to say what I always say, and then I shall go home by the stairs, which have never once frightened me.

units.author: dc_12_ollie
units.text: the roof door was open this morning when i went up to get my football back (dont tell my mum) (she reads this) (sorry mum). it was just open with nobody there and the wind coming in. its meant to have a bar across it. i shut it. is that allowed

units.author: dc_11_soraya
units.text: Thank you for tonight, Bev. It helped to hear other people say what they had heard without anybody laughing. R. was with me, sorry he fell asleep on the biscuit table. He told Mrs Irena that the man on the stairs is 'not on 7 tonight'. I don't know where he gets it from. Soraya, 11F

units.author: dc_8_benedikt
units.text: I played the recording at the meeting on Hassan's speaker. Some people say fridge, some say steps. Mr Pryce says hysteria. I say again for the notes: there isn't a fridge on that floor. I looked again tonight. Thank you for the biscuits, Hassan, they were the good ones.

units.title: Residents' meeting, day 8: notes
units.author: dellow_admin
units.text: Quick notes from tonight, proper minutes to follow when the print shop calms down: 23 of us, plus Hassan's biscuits. 1. Stairwell lights 6-8: the Association will write to Kerrow formally, with Irena's list attached. 2. Lift: engineer booked for tomorrow, we'll believe it when we see it. 3. Until it's all fixed, nobody should feel they have to use the stairs alone at night: there's a buddy sheet by the post boxes. 4. Please don't prop the fire doors. Bev, DCRA

units.author: dellow_admin
units.text: 5. Thanks to Benedikt for playing his recording. People heard different things, and that's fine. Please don't share it outside the building without his say-so. 6. Some children are frightening each other at school about 'the man on the stairs'. Please have a gentle word at home. 7. Bins on 3: noted, Wendell, and added to the letter. Bev

units.author: dc_9_tobin
units.text: For the notes, my method on the recording, since people asked at the meeting. 1. Onsets marked by software. 2. Each onset checked by eye against the waveform. 3. Benedikt's own steps excluded using the sound of his keys. 4. One number will be posted with its method, not before. 19 per flight, two flights. Expected value: 38.

units.author: dc_6_jordie
units.text: went to the meeting for the biscuits, stayed for the bit where bev said 'please stop making memes about the stairwell', which was fair. stairs were quiet tonight. took them with ivy who was going up to draw and we talked loudly the whole way like idiots. 10/10 would recommend. also tobin is going to count the ghost's steps, which is the most tobin thing that has ever happened

units.author: dc_14_ivy
units.text: Ollie, I can back you up on this one. I go up to the top landing to draw the city at night, and the roof door is sometimes on the latch in the mornings, not barred. I assumed the caretaker (still never met the caretaker). I am beginning to think 'the caretaker' covers a lot of things in this building.

units.author: dc_5_lorna
units.text: I couldn't come to the meeting love because I was at the depot but thank you Bev for the notes, and I've put my name on the buddy sheet for mornings, so anyone coming home around five can walk up with me, I talk the whole way so you won't hear a thing except me

units.author: hobby_tapeloop
units.text: Dear all, a lovely recording, Odile. In my day we said fog 'closes the lid'. On tape, damp weather also does curious things to the oxide, so if anyone is recording to cassette this week, please keep the tapes somewhere dry and warm. A question for the young people: how does one attach a picture to a reply? Regards, Ned

units.author: hobby_binaural
units.text: Thank you, Ned! There's a little paperclip under the reply box, bottom left. If it doesn't work for you, send the picture to me and I'll post it with your name on. I would love to see the old machines. Headphones on, always.

units.author: dc_8_benedikt
units.text: Raw file is up now, from the old phone, 4 min 12 s, 48 kHz. Same night, day 5, 23:10. You can hear my keys at the start. Please be careful with it, my voice is in it at the end saying a bad word when I drop the keys.

units.author: brackwater_keeper
units.text: Valve works or no valve works, I walked the dam at half nine tonight and the water engineers have a van parked by the outflow with a work lamp on it. If you are recording out there, you are recording them, and their generator, and their radio. Stay off the bank.

units.author: dc_9_tobin
units.text: Received, thank you. First pass: impacts are clearly separable from 0:41 to 2:58. I will not post a number yet. Method as stated on the Dellow board: onset detection, a manual check of every onset, Benedikt's own steps excluded by his keys. Expect a count in a few days, with a table.

units.title: Night 7: the recorder I left running caught five knocks
units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: Correction to last night's 'nothing'. When I packed up at 02:30 I left the handheld running on the east ride post, gain -18, low cut at 80 Hz. Listening back today: five knocks between 02:40 and 03:08, single, dull, about seven minutes apart, all from roughly the same bearing toward the reservoir. Raw WAV up, unedited. Make of it what you will.

units.author: hobby_binaural
units.text: On the raw file the localisation is clearer. Steps 23 to 30 come from above and slightly behind on the left, and they move. Hollis, reflections usually make a sound diffuse; they don't normally give you a clean image that travels. To be fair, I'll test it in my own stairwell at home.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Please do test it. Concrete risers can make clean false images, because the reflections are strong and arrive early. Separately: the raw file confirms the 58 Hz, and it is louder on this copy. Cycle is 41 s on, 14 s off, throughout, including while Benedikt stands still. A compressor is running somewhere near that mic.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: ok so this is weird. I left my cheap recorder strapped to the gate of the old pumping house overnight too, 300 m east of dunlin's post, to catch the valve works. I've got knocks as well, five of them, first at 02:41:12, and each one lands the same gap after one of his, every time. like an answer from further off. clocks synced from my phone at 21:00, I checked. spectrogram attached, with arrows, sorry about the arrows

units.author: dc_8_benedikt
units.text: Then where is it? There isn't a fridge on that floor. Tonight I opened the bin store with the torch and stood and listened. Bins. Nothing humming. I was there five minutes. A neighbour from 8C asked what I was doing and I could not explain well.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Quick analysis before this becomes a story. The gap is about 61.5 s on all five. A constant offset across every event is what a clock error looks like, not an answer. Sound covers 300 m in about 0.87 s, so one knock heard at both posts arrives under a second apart. Take off a minute and you're left with about a second and a half. Check the clocks.

units.author: lowband_mod
units.text: Pinning this one next to the original knock thread. Good practice from both of you: raw files, settings, times, positions. Please keep doing exactly that, and please everyone else resist the urge to name it. Mod.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: both recorders were synced to my phone at 21:00, I watched the seconds tick over on both screens. and even if you take a minute off, that leaves a beat and a half after each of his, which is still an answer?? also mine have two parts, a knock and then a softer knock, his are single. I'm sure about the clocks. ok fairly sure. no, I'm sure

units.author: hobby_hydrophone
units.text: Two-part thud beside a pumping house on a reservoir main during valve works. That's a check valve slamming and then the pipe ringing. The works were running 22:00 to 05:00 by the council's own notice. I'd put money on it.

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: The valve works are in my log column, and yes, they were running. On my file the works are a continuous hiss near the dam; the knocks are separate and don't change when the hiss does. I'm not claiming anything about tern's gap until the clocks are checked. Two recorders, cheap clocks, 300 m. I'd want a third recorder before I believed in an answer. Make of it what you will.

units.author: nightscream_vlog
units.text: answering knocks guys. answering. this is the clip of the year. im making a video about it whether you like it or not, its public, you posted it

units.title: Dead-air caller, same minute every night
units.author: lh_callcentre_tamsin
units.text: ok so, between calls. For six nights now I get a call at 03:17 on the dot from the same number. Dead air. Not breathing, not hold music, just an open line. Script says 'I can't hear you, I'm going to end the call now', so I do. It never rings back. Same minute every time. Supervisor says it's 'one of those'.

units.author: lh_callcentre_tamsin
units.text: part two because a caller came in about a gas meter that sings: the number is a landline on our local exchange. I'm not allowed to look it up. I am apparently allowed to complain about it on a forum during my break, which is what this is

units.title: Coffee rules for the long haul
units.author: lh_trucker_orrin
units.text: Coffee rules from forty years of nights, for the new folks. One cup at the start, one at the halfway, none in the last two hours or you'll lie in the sleeper staring at the roof. Stretch at every fuel stop, even if you don't need fuel. And if you can't remember the last ten miles, pull in. The road will wait for you.

units.author: lh_kennel_orrin
units.text: Pete popped the ceiling tile over the back corridor vent. Dust, a lot of it, and an old fan motor that runs warm. He cleaned it out. Biscuit still sat at the door at 02:15. Juno walked through fine this time, then wouldn't come back the same way and went round by the front. Dmitra's smell idea is still on my list.

units.author: lh_student_kestrel
units.text: update: emailed facilities at 1am (they will love me). checked: the panels are all on one circuit. also tonight only the far panel came on and nothing else did, then off. so maybe it cascades sometimes and sometimes not? I had been awake 19 hours, Dmitra, you were right to ask, I did not enjoy being asked

units.author: lh_convenience_kestrel
units.text: update from the shop: she bought the banana. she also bought three energy drinks and a family-size bag of crisps. progress is not linear.

units.author: lh_mod
units.text: Housekeeping, small one: please don't post the number, Hana, not even part of it. If it keeps happening, your team leader can ask the carrier to trace it, which is their job and not ours. Hope the singing gas meter is all right. Ines

units.author: lh_dockguard_coriveth
units.text: Log: quiet night. Monitor 6 clear all shift. 02:30 a fox crossed the NE corner in the floodlight, on camera and on foot both at once, which was reassuring. IT ticket raised for the persistence setting. Patrolled, nil found.

units.author: lh_baker_coriveth
units.text: No van tonight. The street felt oddly empty without it, which is a ridiculous thing to say about a van. Croissants were very good, the butter finally behaving now it has turned cold. The gate 7 man got his rolls warm for once.

units.title: Clear night up top
units.author: lh_crane_halvard
units.text: Clear night from the cab after a week of murk over the river. Sixty metres up you see the whole city lit like a circuit board, the ring road, the hospital, the dark bit where the park is. Night lift at 01:00, a roof plant unit. Question for everyone: what's the first thing you see when you look out at work at night?

units.author: lh_dockguard_coriveth
units.text: The monitor wall, nine screens. Then the floodlit lot through the gatehouse glass. Then the dark past the fence, where the cranes are parked with their booms up like they're listening.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: Dogs can smell a dead rodent in a wall cavity long before we can. If the fan pushed air down that corridor, it may have pushed something else along with the dust. Worth a nose at the vent outlet, gloves on. Juno going round the long way is a very dog solution.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: A single panel firing on its own is classic for a sensor near a vent or a door with a draught under it. Sleep, then see if it still bothers you. I mean that kindly, and I mean it for everyone who reads this at their desk at three.

units.author: lh_carer_vellmark
units.text: Last night, nothing at 03:10. Mrs A. slept right through. I sat near the door anyway, which my partner says is the opposite of the point. Maintenance has put the junction box on their list for 'next week'. I made her toast at six and she asked if anyone had come.

units.title: Something is moving through the night shifts...
units.author: hollow_signal
units.text: I won't say much... but count the reports this week. Vans that don't leave. Corridors the dogs won't walk. Monitors that see what the guards don't. Phones that ring with nobody there. Some of us were told to watch for exactly this. You'll understand in a few weeks.

units.author: skeptic_orla
units.text: Autodiallers do exactly this. A sales system dials, finds no free agent on its own end, drops you into silence, logs you as 'contacted' and moves on. Same minute every night because the campaign starts at the same minute. We get them on the studio line. Source: the studio line, every night at 01:58.

units.author: lh_porter_portammet
units.text: We had one on the porters' lodge phone for a month. It turned out to be the lift alarm in the old wing dialling out at the same time every night, because its battery test ran on a timer. Not saying that's yours. Saying check whether any machines in your building know your number.

units.author: lh_porter_portammet
units.text: The car park from the B corridor window, with the ambulance bay lit up orange. Then my own reflection in the glass, looking like a man who has pushed a trolley eleven miles tonight.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: Hollow, you were told nothing by anyone. That is five unrelated workplaces in four time zones, with five ordinary explanations at various stages of being checked: a sleeping driver, a warm fan, a camera setting, a damp box, an autodialler. Putting them in a list doesn't connect them. It just makes a list.

units.author: skeptic_orla
units.text: source? Genuine question, Hollow. Who told you, when, and what exactly were you told to watch for? If you cannot say, it is a story, and I hear enough of those on the overnight line.

units.title: Targets
units.author: lh_picker_weyhaven
units.text: rate tonight: 112 percent. reward: a sticker. an actual sticker, with a star on it. the yard floodlights all work for once now the fog has gone, you can see right to the fence, which is nice, because last week the fence was a rumour. back to aisle 41

units.author: lh_mod
units.text: Housekeeping: Hollow, this is a warning. Please don't stitch other people's posts together into predictions. They're people's jobs and their nights, not your evidence. The next one comes down. Ines

units.author: lh_taxi_halvard
units.text: rule five, never accept coffee from a fare who says he made it himself, anyway good list Merle, I break three of them every night and I've been fine for twenty years apart from the hedge

units.author: lh_security_st
units.text: Can confirm from across the yard, the fence exists. Control has asked me to stop calling the van 'my van' on the radio. It wasn't there tonight. Neither was a sticker for me. I'd like a sticker.

units.author: lh_nurse_halvard
units.text: Rule six: water, as Ines says. Rule seven: eat something green that isn't a sweet. Rule eight: if a colleague says you look tired, believe them. Lovely list, Merle. Back to it.

units.title: What I'm reading at three in the morning
units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: Reading an old book about lighthouse keepers that came in a job lot from a house clearance. Every chapter opens with the weather. I find this enormously comforting. It is clear in Tollinby at last; I can see Orion over the church, slightly crooked as always, as if somebody hung him in a hurry.

units.author: lh_miner_vellmark
units.text: Rock. Then the lamp on the next man's helmet. Then rock again. Good question though, crane man. Up top on the bus home it's the town's lights coming on as the day shift wakes, one window then another.

units.author: lh_lighttender_tamsin
units.text: The lamp itself, from the inside, which is a strange thing to look at for a living: a slow bright wheel with you at its hub. Then the sea, which is always darker than the sky by a little, even on the blackest nights.

units.author: dc_5_lorna
units.text: update love they put two new lamps in over the wash bays tonight, two out of eleven, and the supervisor said 'there you are then' like he'd done it himself, still we could see the back seats on the 14s for once and found a whole loaf and a lady's umbrella in one
